title: Boris — 4yo ferret: staring episodes and hind-limb weakness
presentation: 4-year-old male neutered ferret with three weeks of episodes: he stares blankly, drools, then drags his hind legs for a few minutes before recovering. Worse first thing in the morning and after play.

stages.title: Read the pattern of the episodes
stages.briefing: Weight 1.1 kg, BCS 4/9, lost 200 g since last year. During an episode in the consulting room: obtunded, ptyalism, pawing at the mouth, hind-limb ataxia, no loss of consciousness and no tonic-clonic activity. Recovers over five minutes. Temperature 37.8°C. Abdominal palpation: no organ enlargement, no splenomegaly. Adrenal region not palpable.
stages.prompt: Which features point to a metabolic rather than a primary neurological cause?

options.label: Episodes worse after fasting overnight and after exercise
options.detail: Classic timing for hypoglycaemia

options.label: Ptyalism with pawing at the mouth during episodes
options.detail: Nausea of hypoglycaemia, a well-described ferret sign

options.label: Full recovery between episodes
options.detail: Episodic dysfunction rather than a fixed lesion

options.label: Weight loss of 200 g
options.detail: Real, but non-specific in a four-year-old ferret

options.label: Temperature 37.8°C
options.detail: Normal for a ferret

stages.explanation: The timing is the diagnosis in waiting: signs that appear after a fast and after exertion, and resolve completely, describe a substrate problem rather than a structural one. Ptyalism and mouth-pawing are what a hypoglycaemic ferret does, and every clinician who has seen one recognises it. The weight loss matters for the differential list but discriminates nothing on its own.

stages.title: Test the hypothesis
stages.briefing: You want the answer today. The ferret last ate four hours ago and is currently between episodes.

options.label: Blood glucose during or immediately after an episode
options.detail: The single test that confirms the mechanism

options.label: Paired serum insulin on the same hypoglycaemic sample
options.detail: Inappropriate insulin against a low glucose

options.label: Full biochemistry including urea, ALT and albumin
options.detail: Hepatic and renal causes of hypoglycaemia

options.label: Haematology
options.detail: Screens for the other ferret neoplasias

options.label: Abdominal ultrasound of the pancreas and adrenals
options.detail: Nodules are often too small to see, but adrenal disease is the co-traveller

options.label: Adrenocorticotropic hormone stimulation test
options.detail: Ferret adrenal disease is a sex-steroid disease; this is the wrong axis

options.label: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis
options.detail: Invasive, and not what an episodic, fully reversible picture calls for

stages.explanation: A glucose taken during signs is worth more than any imaging: the case turns on documenting hypoglycaemia and then showing insulin that has no business being measurable at that glucose. Sampling between episodes is the common error — a normal reading then excludes nothing. Ultrasound is worth doing while knowing that a normal pancreas does not rule an insulinoma out.

stages.title: Interpret the results
stages.briefing: Blood glucose during an episode 1.8 mmol/L (32 mg/dL; ref 5.0–11.7). Paired insulin 320 pmol/L — measurable, and inappropriate at that glucose. ALT 68 U/L, albumin 32 g/L, urea 6.4 mmol/L, all within reference. Ultrasound: pancreas unremarkable, left adrenal 6 mm and mildly rounded. Haematology unremarkable.

options.label: Pancreatic beta-cell tumour (insulinoma)
options.detail: Hypoglycaemia with inappropriate insulin

options.label: Concurrent adrenal disease
options.detail: A rounded left adrenal in a ferret of this age, common alongside

options.label: Hepatic insufficiency
options.detail: Normal albumin, urea and ALT

options.label: Sepsis-associated hypoglycaemia
options.detail: No fever, normal white cell count, three weeks of episodes

options.label: Idiopathic epilepsy
options.detail: Does not explain a glucose of 1.8 mmol/L

stages.explanation: Measurable insulin against a glucose of 1.8 mmol/L is the diagnosis: a normal pancreas secretes almost nothing at that level. Normal liver markers and a normal white cell count remove the two mimics that would have changed the plan. The adrenal note is not incidental — ferrets collect endocrine neoplasia, and missing the second one means a partial response later.

stages.title: Commit to a diagnosis
stages.briefing: Glucose 1.8 mmol/L with paired insulin 320 pmol/L, normal hepatic and renal markers, no sepsis, mildly rounded left adrenal.

options.label: Insulinoma, with suspected concurrent adrenal disease
options.detail: Inappropriate insulin at a documented low glucose

options.label: Hypoglycaemia secondary to hepatic dysfunction
options.detail: Contradicted by normal albumin, urea and ALT

options.label: Idiopathic epilepsy
options.detail: A glucose of 1.8 mmol/L is not idiopathic anything

options.label: Adrenal disease alone
options.detail: Ferret adrenal disease causes alopecia and pruritus, not hypoglycaemia

options.label: Lymphoma with paraneoplastic hypoglycaemia
options.detail: Described, but the paired insulin points squarely at beta cells

stages.explanation: The pairing is what earns the diagnosis — glucose and insulin from the same tube, at the same moment. It commits you to frequent protein-rich meals, prednisolone or diazoxide, and a conversation about surgery, and the flagged adrenal keeps you looking when the alopecia arrives in six months.
